keySentence: Integrity means being honest even when costly — Pinocchio paid a very high price to learn.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio did not learn honesty from a book or a lecture. He learned it through painful experience over a long time. He was put in prison and almost drowned in the sea. A giant shark swallowed him with his father still inside. Every disaster could be traced back to one of his lies. The price of dishonesty was extremely high in the end. The price of honesty turned out to be far smaller than he thought. Integrity means being honest even when costly — Pinocchio paid a very high price to learn.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio's education in honesty was not delivered in a classroom or through wise words alone. It came through direct and often very painful experience accumulated over a long period of time. He was imprisoned, nearly drowned, swallowed by a shark, and lost his father inside that shark. Every one of these disasters could be traced back directly to a moment when he had chosen to lie. The price of dishonesty turned out to be extraordinarily high when you added it all together. And the price of honesty — a moment of embarrassment, a short punishment, a difficult conversation — turned out to be far smaller and far more manageable than he had always imagined it would be. Integrity means being honest even when costly — Pinocchio paid a very high price to learn.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio's real education in honesty was not delivered to him in a classroom or transmitted through wise and carefully spoken words alone. It came to him, instead, through direct and often extraordinarily painful experience, accumulated slowly and expensively over a very long period of time. He was imprisoned for being the victim of a crime rather than its perpetrator, he was nearly drowned in the cold Mediterranean Sea, and he was eventually swallowed whole by an enormous shark. Inside the shark he was reunited with his lost father Geppetto, who had been searching for him and had himself been swallowed during a terrible storm at sea. Every one of these disasters, traced carefully back to their beginnings, could be connected directly to a specific moment when Pinocchio had chosen a small and convenient lie over the truth. The total price of his dishonesty, when you added it all up, turned out to be extraordinarily and almost unbelievably high when compared to what he had originally thought he was saving. And the price of honesty — a moment of embarrassment, a short punishment, a single difficult conversation with someone who loved him — turned out to be far, far smaller. By the end of the long lesson, Pinocchio had learned the difference in a way that no classroom lecture could ever have taught him. Integrity means being honest even when costly — Pinocchio paid a very high price to learn.
